recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16347; reconcile related datatype issues only under their own keys if selected separately.
issue_request: FHIR-16347 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the STU3 datatype page and asked whether instant is only for server/system timestamps or can also be used by clinical or administrative resources such as Appointment and Observation. The resolution was to clarify that instant is suitable anywhere a work group decides a full instant of time is required, as opposed to merely allowed by dateTime.
initial_application: The SVN-backed git commit 077b0ff042befbd4c6611c1f3969cccaea79b5a3, with message "GF#16347 - note about use of instant" and git-svn revision 14163, applied the issue by adding the note that instant is intended when precisely observed times are required and not for human-reported times.
additional_context: The active datatype page still contains the clarification, the primitive spreadsheet source carries matching instant guidance, and the current Appointment and Observation definitions do not show a remaining inconsistency that would require this seed to change source. Related FHIR-16274, FHIR-16944, FHIR-42984, and FHIR-24564 refine adjacent questions without superseding the seed resolution.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the current FHIR source already satisfies the requested clarification.
